articles.title: Building AI Agents That Actually Understand the Web: Why Search Infrastructure Matters
articles.excerpt: Building AI Agents That Actually Understand the Web: Why Search Infrastructure Matters AI agents are becoming increasingly capable, but there is still one major limitation that developers frequently u…
articles.body: Building AI Agents That Actually Understand the Web: Why Search Infrastructure Matters AI agents are becoming increasingly capable, but there is still one major limitation that developers frequently underestimate: access to reliable, up-to-date information. An LLM can reason, summarize, generate code, and follow complex instructions. However, its knowledge is fundamentally limited by its training data and the information provided within its context window. This becomes a serious problem when building applications that need current information. Consider an AI research assistant that needs to compare five software products, retrieve their latest pricing, verify product documentation, and produce a report with citations. A language model alone cannot reliably perform this task.

articles.title: The Developer's Field Guide to Google DevFest Atlanta 2026
articles.excerpt: One question stayed with me after Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College: if an AI agent needed to stop right now, could your team prove that it stopped safely? Jim Stephens's session on the…
articles.body: One question stayed with me after Google DevFest Atlanta 2026 at Morehouse College: if an AI agent needed to stop right now, could your team prove that it stopped safely? A lot of the conversation around agentic AI is still focused on how quickly we can build, connect, and automate. But several sessions at DevFest pushed in a different direction: what does it actually take to operate these systems safely once they are doing real work? Jim Stephens's session on the Hidden Constraint Index gave a practical way to think about what is really slowing an organization down. The key reminder for me was that the first diagnosis is not always the real constraint. A team can optimize for speed or adoption and still create problems elsewhere in the system.

articles.title: Snapshot tests for documents
articles.excerpt: A broken document template rarely throws an error. The API returns 200, a PDF is generated, and everything looks fine from the application's point of view. But the document is different from last week…
articles.body: A broken document template rarely throws an error. The API returns 200 , a PDF is generated, and everything looks fine from the application's point of view. But the document is different from last week's: the reverse-charge note is missing, the footer contains outdated bank details, or the total uses the wrong tax rate. The people who notice are the ones receiving the document. That's why testing document templates means checking what they produce, not just whether they render successfully. This post shows how we use snapshot tests to catch unintended changes in generated documents, how to choose the right test data, and what we discovered about our own testing tool along the way. What to compare Not the PDF itself.

articles.title: pgvector for Beginners: Add Semantic Search to PostgreSQL
articles.excerpt: You already have PostgreSQL, backups, and a team that knows how to operate them. Then a new feature asks for semantic search, and suddenly the architecture diagram grows a separate vector database. Fo…
articles.body: You already have PostgreSQL, backups, and a team that knows how to operate them. Then a new feature asks for semantic search, and suddenly the architecture diagram grows a separate vector database. For many applications, that extra system is unnecessary. pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL itself. That means embeddings can live beside the documents, users, and permissions they belong to — with normal transactions, joins, and backups. What an embedding does An embedding model turns text, an image, or another input into a list of numbers. Similar inputs tend to produce vectors that are close together in the model's mathematical space.

articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.body: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. After five years in development at Retro Studios, the original makers of the Metroid Prime series, fans were greeted with annoying side characters, a bike for Samus to roam the barren landscape on, and a deeply unsatisfying ending. It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. Many franchises were jumping from 2D to 3D at the turn of the millennium, and there were plenty of failures — but Metroid wasn’t one of them.

articles.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
